rationale: The hypothesis posits a longitudinal developmental shift in FBXO11-related disorder (IDDFBA) from childhood hyperactive/aggressive dysregulation (ADHD) to adolescent and adult internalizing symptoms (depression, anxiety). While individual longitudinal reports such as Lee et al. (2020) demonstrate childhood ADHD followed by comorbid adolescent/adult depression and anxiety, broader cross-sectional and clinical sequencing cohorts demonstrate persistent externalizing disorders into adolescence (e.g., hyperkinetic disorder in a 14-year-old in Fritzen et al., 2018) and adult presentations retaining ADHD and behavioral dysregulation (Mainali et al., 2023). Furthermore, Jansen et al. (2019) describe anxiety, aggression, and ADHD co-occurring across the wider cohort without establishing an age-dependent transition or extinction of hyperactive symptoms. Thus, the evidence indicates psychiatric comorbidity across the lifespan rather than a deterministic longitudinal transition.

evidence.text: In a familial report of IDDFBA with a novel heterozygous FBXO11 frameshift variant (c.2401_2405dup; p.Gly803Leufs*6), an affected patient was treated for childhood ADHD as well as subsequent depression, illustrating comorbid externalizing and internalizing manifestations over development.

evidence.text: Among 24 individuals with de novo variants or deletions in FBXO11, behavioral disturbances were noted in most patients across a broad spectrum including autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, anxiety, and aggression without demonstrating a strict chronological replacement of hyperactive symptoms by internalizing symptoms.

evidence.text: A 14-year-old adolescent individual with a de novo FBXO11 splice-site variant exhibited persistent hyperkinetic disorder alongside mild ID and microcephaly, contradicting the assertion that childhood hyperactivity resolves or transitions completely before adulthood.

conflicts: Externalizing symptoms (hyperactivity, ADHD, and aggressive behavioral issues) persist into late adolescence (e.g. at 14 years of age in Fritzen et al. 2018) and adulthood (Mainali et al. 2023), contradicting a mandatory evolutionary transition where externalizing traits remit in favor of internalizing symptoms.

Internalizing symptoms (anxiety) and externalizing symptoms (ADHD, aggression) are reported as co-occurring behavioral characteristics in cross-sectional pediatric/adolescent series (Jansen et al. 2019) rather than chronologically separated stages.

new_directions.question_text: Does standardized longitudinal psychiatric assessment in a multi-center cohort of FBXO11 mutation carriers reveal true age-dependent symptom evolution versus lifetime cumulative comorbidity?
new_directions.rationale: Available evidence relies on retrospective chart reviews and cross-sectional snapshots; formal prospective tracking using validated instruments across childhood, adolescence, and adulthood is required to assess whether hyperactivity shifts to depression.

new_directions.question_text: Do truncating loss-of-function versus missense variants in FBXO11 differentially correlate with persistent externalizing ADHD phenotypes versus predominant affective disorders?
new_directions.rationale: Phenotypic heterogeneity across reported cohorts may stem from allelic heterogeneity (missense vs nonsense/frameshift) rather than strictly chronological patient age.
